fixes.explanation: Altars are a good guess, friend. But David doesn't mention building anything in this charge. He tells Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, to "…walk in His ways…" and keep God's commands (1 Kings 2:3).

Rest sounds nice, friend, and I'd take a little myself. But that's not the word in David's charge. He says the goal is that Solomon "…may prosper in all you do and wherever you turn…" (1 Kings 2:3). Prosper is the word to remember.

Yes! David quotes the promise: "…you will never fail to have a man on the throne of Israel." (1 Kings 2:4). The promise is about his descendants sitting on that throne. Here David tells it to his son Solomon as he charges him.

Those are the words. David says, "…show loving devotion to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite…" (1 Kings 2:7). After the heavy part about Joab, this one is a lot warmer. David's instruction for Barzillai's sons is kindness.

It's true, friend! David tells Solomon, "…let them be among those who eat at your table…" (1 Kings 2:7). That's what David wants for Barzillai's sons. He gives his reason: they stood by him when he fled from Absalom.

Yes! David reigned "…seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem." (1 Kings 2:11). Add them up and you get forty years over Israel. I counted it on my mustache twice, friend, and I still needed a minute. Great work!

Forty-seven is the right size of number for a long reign, friend, but it doesn't fit. The verse says forty years in all: "…seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem." (1 Kings 2:11). Seven plus forty-seven would be fifty-four, and that's way more than the verse says.
